title: Bosch Digital Design System and Bosch Brand Guide - Imagery Style Research
intended_use: Grounding AI systems for Bosch-compliant image generation
Supporting UX/UI designers working with Bosch digital touchpoints
Supporting frontend developers implementing image-heavy digital interfaces
Supporting prompt authors creating Bosch visual generation prompts
Supporting design audits for brand-compliant imagery usage

scope.primary_focus: How Bosch imagery style from the Bosch Brand Guide is interpreted and operationalized in Bosch Digital Design System contexts.
imagery_types_covered: visualizations of invisible elements such as AI, data, processes, or energy flows
excluded_or_limited_scope: Full legal interpretation of copyright and AI law
Exact technical production specifications from downloadable PDFs
Division-specific imagery exceptions unless explicitly documented
Full image asset inventory from Bosch Media Asset Management

executive_summary.short_definition: Bosch imagery style is the brand-governed visual language for photographs, product images, explanatory visuals, films, and digital media. It emphasizes authentic, lifelike, modern, high-quality, vivid, and use-oriented representations of Bosch products and environments.
executive_summary.main_conclusion: The Bosch Brand Guide is the upstream authority for imagery style. BDDS does not create a separate imagery language; it operationalizes Bosch imagery principles in digital contexts by requiring brand consistency, accessibility, responsiveness, performance awareness, legal compliance, and component-compatible usage.
key_takeaways: Bosch imagery must feel authentic and lifelike rather than artificial, generic, or over-staged.
The preferred visual storytelling direction is away from isolated product staging and toward real product use in real-life contexts.
Images should use saturated, vivid colors and natural, pleasant lighting and contrast.
Product and technical explanatory imagery should remain focused, reduced, and clear, directing attention to the product or technical message.
Digital usage adds constraints not always visible in print-oriented brand rules: alt text, contrast, responsive cropping, image optimization, machine readability, and accessible implementation.
AI-generated imagery is allowed only under Bosch-approved tool and legal guidance, with additional human review for brand, rights, and quality compliance.
Official Bosch image databases or Media Asset Management sources should be preferred because they help secure licensing and brand-style compliance.

brand_intent.core_intent: Bosch imagery should visually communicate the brand promise of improving life through useful, high-quality, human-centered technology.
strategic_role: Support trust in Bosch products and services
Make Bosch solutions understandable through real use situations
Connect products to benefits and human contexts
Avoid arbitrary, decorative, or generic visual language

Operational platform for living brand documentation, searchable guidelines, templates, assets, and brand governance.

important_relationships.brand_guide_to_bdds: BDDS is a digital extension of the Bosch Brand Guide and should not be treated as a separate visual style language.
important_relationships.bdds_to_implementation: BDDS makes imagery usable in digital products through components, accessibility rules, responsive layout behavior, and design-development alignment.
important_relationships.brand_platform_to_assets: Frontify and related asset platforms provide the operational environment for finding, applying, and maintaining official brand guidance and approved assets.

core_imagery_principles.name: Authentic and lifelike
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Imagery should look real, credible, and grounded in believable situations.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Builds trust and emotional connection by avoiding fake-looking scenes.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Avoid generic stock images, fake-looking AI images, exaggerated staging, and unrealistic interface hero visuals.

core_imagery_principles.name: Real product use over posed product staging
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Images should show Bosch products in meaningful use contexts rather than isolated or decorative product placement.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Connects Bosch products to benefits, people, and real environments.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Hero images, landing pages, product tiles, and digital campaigns should prefer contextual product application images when relevant.

core_imagery_principles.name: Natural, pleasant light and contrast
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Images should have appealing exposure, natural lighting, and comfortable contrast.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Supports a modern, premium, and approachable look.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Images must remain legible when combined with text, UI controls, overlays, and responsive crops.

core_imagery_principles.name: Saturated and vivid colors
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Bosch photography should use strong, lively colors without becoming artificial.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Creates positive perception and supports the lively Bosch visual identity.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Images should harmonize with Bosch color tokens and Supergraphic-derived accent logic, without arbitrary colorfulness.

core_imagery_principles.name: High quality
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Images should be technically sharp, modern, professional, and visually refined.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Avoid pixelated, grainy, poorly compressed, badly cropped, or low-resolution images in UI and presentation contexts.

core_imagery_principles.name: Clear focus and meaningful composition
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Every image should have a clear subject, appealing composition, and purposeful perspective.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Keeps communication direct and avoids visual clutter.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Images must retain their focal point across responsive breakpoints, cards, banners, thumbnails, and mobile crops.

core_imagery_principles.name: Focused technical and product explanatory imagery
core_imagery_principles.meaning: Packshots, close-ups, details, free plates, and 3D renderings should be visually reduced and attention-guiding.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Use reduced visuals for product detail modules, specification areas, explainers, and technical feature sections.

core_imagery_principles.name: Rights and licensing clarity
core_imagery_principles.meaning: All image and film material must have necessary usage rights clarified before use.
core_imagery_principles.brand_implication: Protects Bosch from legal and reputational risks.
core_imagery_principles.digital_implication: Prefer official Bosch Media Asset Management or approved image databases; avoid unverified stock and unclear AI outputs.

do_patterns.rule: Use authentic, lifelike images that feel credible and natural.
do_patterns.rationale: Authenticity is central to Bosch's visual trust and brand credibility.

do_patterns.rule: Show Bosch products in real-life use contexts whenever possible.
do_patterns.rationale: Bosch imagery should move from product-only staging toward product use and human benefit.

do_patterns.rule: Use vivid, saturated, and lively color presence while preserving realism.
do_patterns.rationale: Saturated colors create a lively mood and positive brand perception.

do_patterns.rule: Use natural, pleasant lighting and balanced contrast.
do_patterns.rationale: Natural light and pleasant contrast support quality, readability, and modernity.

do_patterns.rule: Use clear composition, active perspective, and meaningful detail shots.
do_patterns.rationale: A clear focal point helps users understand the product or message quickly.

do_patterns.rule: Use official Bosch image databases or MAM assets when available.
do_patterns.rationale: Official asset sources reduce licensing risk and improve brand compliance.

do_patterns.rule: Provide meaningful alt text or text alternatives for informative images.
do_patterns.rationale: Digital accessibility requires machine-readable alternatives for users who cannot perceive images visually.

do_patterns.rule: Plan images for multiple digital formats and responsive crops.
do_patterns.rationale: Bosch imagery must remain clear and effective across digital aspect ratios and breakpoints.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use artificial, over-staged, or unrealistic scenes.
dont_patterns.risk: Breaks authenticity and makes Bosch communication feel generic or untrustworthy.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use artificial filters, including black-and-white filters, as a default brand treatment.
dont_patterns.risk: Weakens the vivid, natural, and authentic Bosch image style.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use unrealistic composings, collages, or manipulated image combinations that feel fake.
dont_patterns.risk: Undermines lifelike representation and can confuse the message.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use generic stock technology visualizations or generic stock images with arbitrary icons or drawings.
dont_patterns.risk: Creates a non-Bosch, generic, low-trust visual impression.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not overlay graphic effects in a way that distorts the image subject or reduces readability.
dont_patterns.risk: Reduces clarity, accessibility, and brand quality.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use unverified images without clarified rights, licenses, or usage permissions.
dont_patterns.risk: Creates legal, copyright, and brand-governance risk.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not use AI-generated images from non-approved tools without legal consultation.
dont_patterns.risk: Creates copyright, data protection, confidentiality, and brand-compliance risk.

dont_patterns.rule: Do not place important text inside images without accessible alternatives.
dont_patterns.risk: Machines and screen readers cannot reliably parse embedded text, reducing accessibility.

digital_operationalization_via_bdds.bdds_role: BDDS operationalizes Bosch imagery style by embedding brand, accessibility, layout, implementation, and governance constraints into digital touchpoints.

digital_constraints.name: Accessibility
requirements: Provide alt text for meaningful images.
Avoid relying on image-only communication.
Avoid text embedded in images unless text alternatives exist.
Ensure sufficient contrast between image backgrounds and overlaid text or UI controls.
Provide captions or alternatives for audiovisual content when needed.

digital_constraints.name: Responsiveness
requirements: Prepare images for multiple aspect ratios such as 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, and 4:3.
Define focal points to preserve key content across responsive crops.
Avoid using images whose main message is lost on mobile or small components.
Test hero images, thumbnails, cards, and banners across breakpoints.

digital_constraints.name: Performance
requirements: Optimize file sizes without visibly damaging image quality.
Use appropriate image formats for the platform.
Avoid oversized images in small UI components.
Use responsive image delivery when implementation allows.
Preserve visual quality while minimizing loading impact.

digital_constraints.name: Layout compatibility
requirements: Integrate imagery into Bosch layout principles with clear hierarchy and whitespace.
Avoid image placements that compete with typography or core UI controls.
Use images purposefully, not decoratively.
Respect logo and Supergraphic clear-space rules when images are near brand elements.

digital_constraints.name: Color and token compatibility
requirements: Ensure images harmonize with Bosch Digital Color System usage.
Avoid arbitrary colorfulness that conflicts with Bosch accent logic.
Use Bosch accent colors in imagery only as natural, targeted accents when appropriate.
Avoid overusing red as a general UI or imagery accent because red has specific brand relevance.

digital_constraints.name: Component compatibility
requirements: Use BDDS-compatible image components or layout patterns when available.
Avoid custom image treatments that break the system.
Keep image usage consistent across cards, banners, pages, dashboards, and presentation modules.

typical_digital_applications.guidance: Use high-quality authentic imagery with strong focal point, safe crop zones, readable overlay space, and responsive variants.
Use focused product or product-application imagery with clear subject, consistent crop, and no distracting background.
Use reduced visual language, detail shots, close-ups, packshots, or approved 3D renderings to direct attention to the product or concept.
Use authentic Bosch-style imagery combined with clean typography, white or light-gray brand context, and restrained accent use.
Plan for compact formats, strong focal points, minimal text, and readable mobile-first crops.
Use imagery only when it supports the task. Avoid visual noise behind interactive controls, forms, or dense data.

preferred: People using Bosch products in believable situations
Work and living situations that feel real rather than posed
avoid: Artificial studio poses when the context demands realism

preferred: Architecture or contextual backgrounds for portraits
Relevant settings that explain product use
avoid: Environments unrelated to the product or message

preferred: Focused shots of people using Bosch products
avoid: Product-only staging when use context is more appropriate
Decorative product placement without user benefit

technical_and_product_explanatory_motifs.definition: Technical and product explanatory motifs are reduced visual formats used to focus attention on products, product details, product functions, or technical explanations.
principles: Attention directed toward product or technical message
avoid: Generic stock image style with arbitrary icons

visualization_of_invisible_elements.purpose: Make invisible elements such as AI, data, processes, or energy flows visible while preserving the realism and clarity of the image.

pixel_code.role: A subtle white pixel-based visual layer that complements the motif without taking center stage.
principles: Adjusted transparency depending on image brightness
implementation_guidance: Separate motif into foreground and background when needed.
Use foreground and background pixel-code layers when appropriate.
Keep distance from image edge according to pixel-code guidance.
Use masks and opacity adjustments per motif.
Make the pixel layer subtle and supportive.
donts: Do not use circles, lines, or other non-approved pixel shapes.
Do not make pixels too large.
Do not create unstable or unclean grids.
Do not distort the subject with overlays.
Do not set transparency too low or too high.

keras_code.role: A layered visual treatment for invisible elements, tailored to motif, focus point, and intended message.
principles: Transparency and blur increase with distance from focus point
Blue tone must remain aligned with Bosch Blue when used
donts: Do not deviate from Bosch Blue when Bosch Blue is required.

ai_generated_imagery_policy.general_position: AI-generated imagery is a controlled use case. It may be explored only within approved Bosch tool, legal, and brand-governance constraints.
mandatory_rules: Use only AI image-generation tools approved by BD for this purpose.
Follow internal Bosch legal guidance, especially the Legal AI FAQ.
If non-approved tools are considered, consult the responsible C/LS Business Lawyer before use.
AI-generated images must still meet Bosch imagery style: authentic, lifelike, vivid, natural, modern, and high-quality.
AI outputs require human review for artifacts, realism, brand fit, and rights risk.
Do not use AI outputs that imitate protected third-party styles, contain unclear copyrighted elements, or include unverifiable people, logos, or products.
recommended_ai_prompt_constraints: No distorted hands, faces, tools, typography, or logos
No unapproved Bosch logo generation unless the task explicitly requires official brand asset placement by a human
review_checklist: Does the image look authentic and lifelike?
Does it avoid generic stock-photo style?
Is the product or use case understandable?
Are rights and usage conditions clear?
Was the tool approved or legally cleared?
Is the image accessible when used digitally?
Does the image still work after responsive cropping?

core_requirements: Provide alt text for meaningful images.
Use empty alt text only for purely decorative images when semantically appropriate.
Do not embed essential information only inside an image.
Ensure contrast between image background and overlaid typography or UI elements.
Use captions or text alternatives for video and audiovisual content.
Avoid image treatments that impair readability.
Ensure keyboard and screen-reader users can access image-related interactions.

machine_readability.principle: Digital images must be interpretable by assistive technologies when they communicate meaning.
implications: Write concise but meaningful alt text.
Provide structured text for charts, diagrams, or process images.
Avoid image-only buttons or links without labels.
Ensure ARIA labels or accessible names exist for interactive image elements.

mandatory_requirements: Clarify rights of use before using produced, purchased, or AI-generated image and film material.
Prefer official Bosch image databases or Media Asset Management sources.
Respect model releases, product rights, location rights, third-party trademarks, and copyright restrictions.
Consult legal stakeholders for unclear rights, AI-generated content, or non-standard usage.
Do not assume that images found online or generated by AI are safe for Bosch use.
risk_areas: Screenshots or images from third-party sources
AI-generated images with unclear commercial rights
Images containing third-party logos or protected designs
Image reuse outside the licensed context

responsibilities: Select images that pass the Bosch imagery checklist.
Use official image libraries whenever possible.
Plan responsive crops and focal points before handoff.
Provide alt text or image meaning descriptions to developers.
Avoid filters, artificial effects, and generic stock imagery.
Escalate uncertain AI or licensing cases to legal or brand governance.
Use imagery purposefully rather than decoratively.
design_handoff_requirements: Intended crop for desktop, tablet, and mobile
Approved image file or asset link
Fallback behavior if image fails to load

responsibilities: Implement images using BDDS-compatible patterns and components when available.
Preserve designer-approved crops and focal points.
Ensure alt attributes and accessible names are implemented correctly.
Optimize images for performance without visible quality loss.
Use responsive image delivery when possible.
Avoid CSS filters or effects that alter Bosch imagery style.
Ensure overlays and text remain readable across breakpoints.
implementation_anti_patterns: Applying arbitrary blur, neon, or duotone effects
Cropping images so the product or person is cut off
Using background images for meaningful content without alternatives
Serving one oversized image to all devices
Replacing approved images with unapproved assets during implementation

recommended_workflow: Load Bosch Brand Guide and BDDS imagery rules as grounding context.
Generate or retrieve candidate imagery only within approved tools and sources.
Evaluate against accessibility and responsive-use requirements.
Route uncertain cases to brand or legal stakeholders.
Store final approved prompt, image source, and rationale for traceability.
minimum_ai_constraints: Treat the Bosch Brand Guide as upstream authority.
Do not invent a new Bosch image style.
Use real-life contexts, natural light, vivid realistic colors, and high-quality composition.
Avoid artificial filters, black-and-white treatments, neon effects, generic stock style, and unrealistic compositing.
Respect accessibility, responsive layout, and licensing constraints.
Flag uncertainty rather than approving risky imagery automatically.

common_misinterpretations.correction: Authentic means believable and lifelike, but still modern, high-quality, and professionally composed.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Product imagery should always isolate the product.
common_misinterpretations.correction: Bosch imagery often prefers product use contexts because they communicate benefit and real-life relevance.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Saturated colors mean artificial color grading.
common_misinterpretations.correction: Colors should be vivid and lively, but still realistic and natural.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Digital teams can use any image if the layout looks good.
common_misinterpretations.correction: Digital teams must respect Brand Guide imagery rules, BDDS accessibility rules, responsive behavior, performance, and licensing.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: AI-generated images are acceptable if they look good.
common_misinterpretations.correction: AI images require approved tools, legal guidance, rights assessment, brand review, and quality review.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Alt text is optional for images.
common_misinterpretations.correction: Meaningful digital images require text alternatives or accessible descriptions.

common_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Black-and-white images are a safe premium style.
common_misinterpretations.correction: Bosch imagery guidance discourages artificial filters, including black-and-white treatments, unless a specific approved exception applies.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Different business units may apply slightly different visual moods while still claiming Bosch compliance.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Clarify which division-specific deviations are approved and document them separately.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Teams may use non-approved AI tools or outputs with unclear copyright status.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Create a standardized approval workflow and prompt checklist for AI-generated imagery.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Images that work in desktop hero banners may fail on mobile or in cards.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Require responsive crop previews and focal-point metadata during design handoff.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Image-based messages may exclude screen-reader users or users with low vision.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Require alt text, captions, contrast checks, and non-image text alternatives.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Images may be over-compressed or oversized, harming either brand quality or loading performance.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Define technical image export standards for each digital use case.

open_questions_and_risks.risk: Teams may select generic stock images that look polished but not Bosch-specific.
open_questions_and_risks.recommended_action: Prefer MAM assets and maintain a do/don't gallery for common imagery mistakes.

image_and_film_checklist.question: Is the image or film material authentic and lifelike?
Are the colors strong, vivid, and still realistic?
Are light and contrast natural and pleasant?
Is the composition appealing, detailed, and uncluttered?
Is the perspective well chosen, active, and storytelling?
Is the close-up or detail shot focused and meaningful?
Have all necessary rights of use been clarified?
Does the image remain accessible in its digital context?
Does the image remain clear across responsive formats?

prompt_ready_guidance.general_bosch_imagery_prompt_fragment: Use Bosch-compliant imagery style: authentic, lifelike, modern, high-quality photography with natural pleasant lighting, vivid but realistic saturated colors, clear composition, and a real product-use context. Avoid posed product staging, generic stock-photo style, artificial filters, black-and-white treatment, neon effects, unrealistic compositing, excessive blur, and decorative overlays. Preserve clarity, accessibility, and responsive readability.
prompt_ready_guidance.product_application_prompt_fragment: Show the Bosch product being used naturally in a realistic environment by believable people or in a true-to-life use situation. Focus on the benefit and context of use rather than isolated product glamour. Keep the scene vivid, clear, modern, and high-quality.
prompt_ready_guidance.technical_explainer_prompt_fragment: Create a focused, reduced, vivid explanatory visual that directs attention to the product or technical feature. Use clean composition, meaningful close-ups or detail views, and avoid generic technology stock visualizations, arbitrary icons, unrealistic 3D effects, or artificial scenes.
prompt_ready_guidance.ai_image_safety_prompt_fragment: Generate only within approved Bosch AI image-generation tools and legal constraints. Do not imitate protected third-party styles, do not include unverified logos or people, and ensure the final image can pass brand, accessibility, and licensing review.
